# US News Map

> Search digitized American newspapers from the Library of Congress's Chronicling America collection and see where and when a word or phrase was printed. Each matching page is placed on the map where its newspaper was published and counted by date. The site and its JSON API are free and need no sign-in.

The newspaper pages come from Chronicling America (Library of Congress, with the National Endowment for the Humanities); `/v1/meta` has the current page, newspaper and place counts and the dates covered (1736 to 1963). The collection is still being indexed, so counts grow between index versions; [the dataset details page](https://usnewsmap.com/datasets) says how much is searchable now. Coverage is uneven: some states, years and languages have far more digitized pages than others, so compare a count with the number of pages published in the same place and dates before reading much into it. The text is OCR, so older pages have many misspellings and broken words. Where the index has it, a page is also searched by the text of American Stories (a separate extraction of the same newspaper pages), and some pages, such as Japanese-language ones, use OCR this project ran itself; `matched_in` on a result says which text matched, and [OCR credits](https://usnewsmap.com/credits) names the engines and their licences.

## Site

- [Home and search](https://usnewsmap.com/): search results show on a map, with a timeline and a table. A search has its own address, `https://usnewsmap.com/search/<query>`, with filters as query parameters: `https://usnewsmap.com/search/cross-of-gold?from=1896-06-01&to=1896-12-31`. A plain phrase is lowercase with hyphens for spaces (`/search/fifteenth-amendment`). A search with `OR`, `-`, wildcards, other punctuation or a `mode` other than `phrase` keeps its text percent-encoded (`/search/gold%20OR%20silver`). Older `/?q=...` links redirect to these. The site's default `mode` is `phrase`, so `/search/know-nothing` finds the exact phrase "know nothing"; the API without `mode` requires all the words instead, and gives many more matches. The map, timeline and table need JavaScript; to read results as data, use the API below. About a hundred common searches (listed in [the sitemap](https://usnewsmap.com/sitemap.xml) and linked from the home page) also include up to ten of the earliest matching pages, from the place with the most matches, as plain HTML that is readable without JavaScript.
- [Dataset details](https://usnewsmap.com/datasets): the collections in the index, where each comes from, its rights and how it is searched; how many of the downloaded pages are searchable, what the ingest pipeline is doing now, and page counts by state and by language. The same data is JSON at `/v1/status`.
- [Privacy](https://usnewsmap.com/privacy): what the site records. Search words are kept, but never with an IP address or anything else about who searched, and not at all when Do Not Track or Global Privacy Control is on.
- [OCR credits](https://usnewsmap.com/credits): the OCR engines and models behind pages this project read itself, with their licences.

## API

Base URL `https://api.usnewsmap.com/v1`. The same routes answer at `https://usnewsmap.com/v1` and under `/api/v1`. All routes are `GET` and return JSON. Errors are `application/problem+json` (RFC 9457) with a `type`, a `detail` and sometimes a `hint` on how to fix the request. On every route that takes parameters, an unknown or repeated parameter is an error, and an empty one counts as absent. List values such as `state` and `lccn` are comma-separated in one parameter.

- `/v1/meta`: the dates covered (`bounds`), page, newspaper and place counts, the `index_version` and its `published_at`, the query `limits`, `capabilities`, and `languages`: each language code with its name, number of pages and number of newspapers.
- `/v1/aggregate?q=...`: for one search, the total number of matching pages, a count per time bucket, counts per place, and per place per bucket. `series.baseline` gives the pages published in each bucket, matching or not, across the whole country or the `state` values given. It is `null` when `lccn` or `front` is set, because the API has no exact page count to compare with then. Otherwise `baseline` says which pages it counts: `{"languages": [...], "why": ...}`, where `why` is `filter` (your `lang`), `query_language` (an English or Japanese query is compared with pages of newspapers in that language, so an English search's baseline counts English pages) or `all`. Hits are never limited by it: without `lang` they count every matching page.
- `/v1/hits?q=...&place=<place id>`: matching pages from one place, oldest first (`sort=newest`, or `sort=relevant` for most mentions first, which needs `q`), each with text snippets and a link to the page on loc.gov. `/v1/hits` needs either `place` or a single `lccn` (one newspaper). `limit` is 1 to 50 (default 50). When `next_cursor` is not null, pass it as `cursor` to get the next results. When `/v1/meta` has `"browse_pages": true`, `/v1/hits?lccn=<one lccn>` with no `q` lists every page of that newspaper by date (`sort=oldest` or `newest`; the other filters still apply), each with the opening of its text as its snippet. Its `next_cursor` goes on to the newspaper's last page, however many there are, where a search's last page is the one starting at result 10,000. Pass the cursor with the same `sort`. On a later page, `total` counts the pages from that one on. Otherwise `q` is required.
- `/v1/places`: every place as GeoJSON, with its name, state, how precisely it is located (`precision`: `city`, `county` or `state`), its number of newspapers and their languages. Place ids such as `P00001` are what `place` takes.
- `/v1/coverage?from=...&to=...&bucket=...`: pages published in each place per bucket, whether or not they match a search, for turning counts into rates by place. It also takes `state`, `lang` and `v`.
- `/v1/status`: the ingest pipeline's progress.
- `/v1/titles`: every newspaper in the index, with its `lccn`, title, `place_id`, place, state, first and last year, page count and languages. `/v1/titles/<lccn>` returns one. Before searching, check here that the papers you need are in the collection. A town with no title has no local coverage, however you search.
- `/v1/days?q=...&place=<id>[,<id>...]`: matching pages per day for 1 to 20 places, for exact median and quartile dates. Each place has parallel arrays `days` and `hits`; a day is a number of days since 1700-01-01. `total.first_day` and `last_day` in `/v1/aggregate` use the same numbering.
- `/v1/versions`: every index version that was built, and which one is being served.
- `/v1/openapi.json`: an OpenAPI 3.1 description of every route above, with each route's parameters and response schemas.

Search parameters, shared by `/v1/aggregate` and `/v1/hits`:

- `q` (required, except for one newspaper's pages on `/v1/hits` as above): the search, up to 256 characters and 12 terms. Search is case-insensitive, and a hyphen inside a word (`know-nothing`) separates words like a space; a leading `-` excludes a word. Japanese works too, as a phrase of characters. Without `mode`, words are all required, a phrase goes in double quotes, `OR` joins alternatives (up to 4), a leading `-` excludes a word, and `word*` matches words that start with `word`, which needs at least 5 letters (`limits.min_prefix_chars` in `/v1/meta`). Inside a word, after the same number of letters, `?` matches exactly one character and `*` any run of characters, for OCR errors: `presi?ent`, `washi*ton`. A `?` at the end of a word is a question mark. Wildcards don't work inside quotes. `word~ocr` also matches the spellings OCR commonly gives a word (`president~ocr` finds `presldent` and `prefident`), and `2 OF (gold silver bryan)` matches pages with at least 2 of the words or phrases in the parentheses (up to 6 of them; `OF` in capitals). A fraction glyph is one word, so `½` alone matches only pages whose text has the glyph; OCR often reads it as `1/2`, the phrase "1 2", so search `1/2` as well. A number with a fraction, such as `61½`, also matches the pages where OCR read it as `61 1/2` or `611/2` (the phrases "61 1 2" and "611 2"), alone, among other words or in a phrase with no slop (`"wheat 61½"`, or `mode=phrase`), but not in a `near` search.
- `mode`: `phrase`, `all`, `any` or `near`, for a plain list of words. `mode=near` also needs `near`, 1 to 20: how many words apart the terms may be.
- `from`, `to`: dates as `YYYY-MM-DD`. Dates outside `bounds` in `/v1/meta` are moved to the nearest bound.
- `state`: comma-separated two-letter postal codes, such as `GA,SC`.
- `lccn`: comma-separated newspaper ids (Library of Congress control numbers).
- `lang`: comma-separated three-letter language codes from the `languages` list in `/v1/meta`, such as `eng`, `ger` or `spa`.
- `front=true`: front pages only.
- `bucket`: `auto`, `year`, `month`, `week` or `day`.
- `fuzzy`: `1` or `2` matches single words within that many letter edits, for OCR errors. It does not apply to phrases (so not to `mode=phrase` or `mode=near`) or to `word*`; those stay exact. It only works when `capabilities.fuzzy` in `/v1/meta` is `true`; otherwise the API answers `422` (`/errors/unsupported`).
- `v`: an `index_version`. If it is not the one being served, the API redirects (307) to the current one. Pass the one `/v1/meta` names: responses are fixed for a version, and without `v` they are cacheable for only 5 minutes.
- `source`: `news` (the default), `congress` or `all`; `series` narrows Congress. Searching Congress is not available yet: `congress` and `all` answer `422` (`/errors/unsupported`) until `congress` in `/v1/meta` is not `null`. `format` is only `json`.

## Response shapes

- `/v1/aggregate`: `total` has the counts (`hits` pages, `papers`, `places`, `days`, `baseline_pages`), `first_day` and `last_day`, and the `first` and `last` matching pages, each shaped like an `/v1/hits` item (below), with `snippets`; `american_stories_only` counts matches found only in American Stories' text. `places` and `papers` hold parallel arrays: `places.id[i]` goes with `places.hits[i]`, and `papers.lccn[i]` with `papers.title[i]` and `papers.hits[i]`. `languages` counts the matching pages per language (`code` and `hits`; `by` is `page` when each page's own language was used, and absent when its newspaper's was). `series` has `hits` and `baseline` per time bucket, and `bucket` says which buckets they are. `cube` is the sparse place by bucket grid, as parallel arrays `p` (an index into `places.id`), `b` (a bucket index) and `h` (hits); when there would be too many cells, `coarsened` is set and the buckets are wider than you asked.
- `/v1/hits`: the pages are in `items`, each with `doc_id`, `date`, `title`, `lccn`, `place_id`, `edition`, `seq`, `front_page`, `snippets` (matches wrapped in `<mark>`, HTML-escaped), `matched_in` (which texts matched: `loc`, `american_stories`, `loc_original`; when the index has them) and `links.viewer`, the page on loc.gov, which opens with the search highlighted. `total` counts every match for this place or newspaper, `days` the days they fall on, and `next_cursor` continues the list. A search stops at result 10,000, so split a larger one by dates, `lccn` or `state`.
- A `doc_id` such as `sn83045462_1865-03-21_ed-1_seq-2` is the newspaper's `lccn`, the date, the edition and the page.

## Research recipe

To find every page about a subject:

1. Run one `/v1/aggregate` with the widest sensible dates and `bucket=year`. `total.hits` says how many pages match, and `total.first` is the earliest matching page.
2. For each id in `places.id` (or each `lccn` in `papers.lccn`), call `/v1/hits` with the same `q`, dates and filters, and follow `next_cursor` until it is `null`.
3. Keep the requests sequential and handle `429`, `202` and `503` as described below. Don't send them in parallel.

Searching for a person:

- Search the surname with one context word, such as a regiment, battle, town or office (`Kuder Waynesboro`, `Kuder "Livingston county"`), rather than the full name in quotes. OCR often misreads initials and ordinals: "Lieut. A. Kuder, 8th N. Y. cavalry" can come out as "Lieut. S. Kuder. Sth N. Y. cavalry", which `"Andrew Kuder"` or `"8th New York"` won't find.
- Try the titles and spellings papers used: `"Lieutenant Kuder"`, `"Lieut. Kuder"`, `"Capt. Kuder"`.
- `word~ocr` and `fuzzy` widen a search for OCR errors, but they are slower than a plain search. Use them on a narrow date range or with a filter.
- Read the snippets before counting a page. A common surname also matches other people with that name, and a search for a name and a town finds every page where both appear, even when they are unrelated.
- Check `/v1/titles` for the person's hometown papers. Chronicling America covers only some of each state's papers, so an obituary or a hometown report may not be in the collection.

## API usage guidelines

- Requests are rate limited per client address. A `429` comes with a `Retry-After` header; wait that many seconds before trying again. A `503` also has `Retry-After`; read its problem `type` and `hint`. `/errors/busy` means wait and send the same request again. `/errors/backend-timeout` means the search did not finish in time: narrow the dates or add filters before retrying, rather than repeating the same request.
- A search nobody has run recently can take a while. The API then answers `202` with `{"status":"computing"}` and a `Retry-After` of a few seconds, and keeps working on it. Send the same request again after that wait to get the result. Results are cached, so a repeated request is cheap.
- Prefer one `/v1/aggregate` request with a wide date range and a coarse `bucket` (such as `year`) over many narrow ones.
- Link people to the loc.gov pages that `/v1/hits` returns, so they can read the original newspaper.
